Advances: ancora.gate

Severity: Medium/Low (calibrated). Consolidated findings F21, F39, F40, F41, F43, F44, F45, F46, F47, F48, F63.

Read this framing first. The simplicity reviewer named the pattern underneath most of these: the rewrite characteristic defect is UNFINISHED SUBSTITUTION, not complexity carried over from specled_ex. Ancora.Json, Ancora.TempName, Output.config_diagnostic/1 and the ETS memo were each written, tested, and then never wired in, while the code that needed them hand-rolls its own version alongside. In one case (review/spec_diff.ex:32) the hand-rolled version reproduces the exact VM-local temp-name collision TempName was written to prevent.

F40 — the verdict pass predicate is written twice: Output.passed?/1 at output.ex:282 and Verdict.pass?/3 at verdict.ex:55, same three branches, same literals. One decides the exit code, the other the printed result token. A divergence prints a passing result while exiting non-zero, which is exactly what the ancora.tasks subject exists to prevent. Promote Verdict.pass?/1 to public and delete the copy.
F21 — use TempName.cross_vm_suffix/0 in BaseView.unique_temp/0, and prefer File.mkdir/1 over File.mkdir_p!/1 so a pre-placed symlink errors instead of redirecting the write. The spec_diff.ex:32 site disappears with F41.
F45 — point Config.emit_config/1, both Severity sites and Trailer.warn/2 at Output.config_diagnostic/1, and extend forbidden_writer_test to cover the stderr diagnostic channel.
F47 — route Output.json_payload/1 through Ancora.Json.encode!/1 so the module is the single encoding point its name implies, matching how Ancora.Git is the single spawner. Do NOT delete it; it is published on hexdocs.
F41 — delete SpecDiff.compute/3 and parse_source/1, and FindingsDelta.compute/3 plus the binary clause of classify/3. This changes the function set that ancora.review tagged tests call, so re-run the gate against main afterwards.
F39 — add a status option to Next.build/2 and have Prime.build/2 pass its already-computed status through, so spec.prime stops running the derivation twice.
F43 — drop the unused change_set parameter from derive_sets/7 and its throwaway binding line, and hoist the single Compare.compare/4 call out of the acknowledgment fork so the rule reads as the filter it is.
F44 — change the resolve/3 typespec third argument from a bare map to Derive.resolver_context().
F46 — have Preflight.project_opts/1 always pass lib_paths, including nil, so ProjectInfo stops re-reading the config, and fix the comment that claims it already does.
F48 — correct the Ancora.ModalClass moduledoc, which states something false about the running system, and pin its phrase regexes to a module attribute if it is kept.
F63 — delete the stale L12 stage marker from the published Ancora.Parser moduledoc.

Deliberately NOT taken, the review dropped them: inlining all_findings/11 and extracting Severity.partition/2, both of which restructure the gate central assembly path for readability alone.

SCOPE ADDITION (orchestrator, 2026-09-03 21:05), from the ancora-xla.2 Elixir test critic. This ticket's subject is finishing half-wired substitutions, and this is one.

test/support/tmp_git_repo.exs:33-46. The cleanup!/1 "poll" added by ancora-xla.2 never iterates. File.rm_rf(root) runs first with zero delay and succeeds, so File.exists?(root) is immediately false and the receive-after block is dead code. The net effect is deleting the 30 millisecond grace, not replacing it with a poll. Ticket item (7) on that ticket asked for a poll instead of a sleep and got a no-op in substance.

It is a measured regression, not a suspicion. The critic ran git_test.exs three times at 420fb94 and counted "fatal: not a git repository" on stderr 3, 1 and 3 times; three runs of the same file with only the base version of tmp_git_repo.exs restored printed it 0, 0 and 0 times. Nothing flakes and no test lies, which is why it was not a merge blocker, but the suite got noisier under the banner of an improvement.

Two honest fixes, implementer's choice: wait on the git child's exit before rm_rf, which is what the poll was trying to express, or restore the sleep with its explanatory comment intact. Do not ship a third variant that also does nothing. Whichever you pick, verify by counting stderr occurrences across at least three runs and report the counts, naming the two states you compared.

Added to Allowed touches: test/support/tmp_git_repo.exs.

Also from the same review, and a natural fit here since it is the same class of half-finished work: test/ancora/derive/pipeline_test.exs:161-168 hand-builds a resolver context map instead of building the real one and overriding a single injection point. The one-line shape the critic gives, matching what the module already does at :30, is to call Derive.context/3 and then replace only the membership function with the raising closure. Line 179's trailing `assert Process.alive?(self())` is a tautology and should be deleted outright; the real proof is that an error tuple is returned at all.

TEST_CRITIC: FAIL

One test does not hold the contract it names. Everything else in the diff holds, and three of the four tests I was asked to treat with suspicion turned out to be sound under execution, not just under reading.

## Blocking

review_test.exs:126 "removed root-reading review entry points stay absent" -- one of the two entry points it names is guarded by a vacuous line.

  refute function_exported?(Ancora.Review.SpecDiff, :compute, 3)   # sound
  refute function_exported?(FindingsDelta, :compute, 3)            # VACUOUS

function_exported?/3 returns false for a module that is not loaded. The SpecDiff refute is fine because the line above it calls SpecDiff.compute(head, nil), which loads the module. Nothing in the test loads FindingsDelta before its refute; the alias at the top of the file does not load, and compiling a test file that contains a FindingsDelta call does not load it either.

I verified this by execution rather than by reading. A probe test file with `alias Ancora.Review.FindingsDelta` plus a later FindingsDelta.classify/3 call reported, at test time:

  PROBE loaded=false
  PROBE fe_compute3=false
  PROBE fe_classify3=false

classify/3 exists. function_exported? still said false. So in an isolated run (mix test test/ancora/review_test.exs:126) the FindingsDelta refute passes no matter what is in the module. In a full-suite run it passes or fails depending on whether some earlier test happened to load FindingsDelta first, which is seed-dependent.

Why it matters: ancora.review.findings_delta_without_store is priority must, and the statement this commit added names three things -- SpecDiff root-reading compute/3, FindingsDelta compute/3, and the binary-root classify/3 clause. Two are guarded. FindingsDelta.compute/3 is not. Reintroducing a path-based compute/3 without touching classify slips through.

The sibling assert_raise FunctionClauseError on FindingsDelta.classify("base-root", "head-root", []) IS sound -- calling the function loads it -- and it does pin the binary-root clause half.

Fix is one line before the refutes:

  Code.ensure_loaded!(Ancora.Review.FindingsDelta)

Worth doing the same for SpecDiff so the guard does not depend on assertion order.

## On the three call_count trace tests: they hold

output_test.exs (Ancora.Json.encode!/1), prime_test.exs (Ancora.Status.build/2), project_info_test.exs (Ancora.Config.load/1).

These are NOT the vacuous self-trace failure mode from the two earlier reviews. That failure mode was :erlang.trace/3 message delivery with refute_received, where a mechanism that never fires makes the refute pass. These use :erlang.trace_pattern(MFA, true, [:call_count]) and read the counter synchronously with :erlang.trace_info/2. call_count is a VM-global counter, needs no tracer process, and every assertion is an equality on the delta (== 1). A mechanism that never fires yields 0 and FAILS. Fail-closed in every direction I could find:

- MFA does not exist -> trace_info returns {:call_count, :undefined}, which still matches the pattern, then arithmetic on the atom raises. Test errors, does not pass.
- on_exit disabling the pattern runs in a separate process, which is correct here because trace_pattern is global, not process-scoped.

All three passed in my run, which is positive evidence the counters incremented exactly once each -- reachability established by execution, not asserted from reading.

Discrimination, checked against the source:

- Config.load/1 has exactly two arity-1 call sites in lib: gate/preflight.ex:22 and project_info.ex:156. Reverting project_opts/1 to the old `defp project_opts(%Config{lib_paths: nil}), do: []` gives delta 2 and the assert fails. Status calls load/2, not load/1, so it cannot contaminate.
- Status.build/2: without Keyword.put(opts, :status, status) in Prime, Next rebuilds and the delta is 2.
- Json.encode!/1: encoding through Jason directly gives 0.

Both prime_test and project_info_test correctly switched to async: false. That is required, not cosmetic -- call_count is VM-global, and ExUnit runs sync modules serially after all async ones, so there is no overlap window. output_test was already async: false.

project_info_test also has a non-trace guard for its must: assert preflight.project.lib_paths == ["lib", "extra"] fails without the new {:ok, nil} clause in ProjectInfo, because validate_lib_paths(nil) returns {:env, ...} and the {:ok, preflight} match breaks first.

## Per-test verdicts

HOLDS -- pipeline_test "a raising resolver returns an error without exiting its caller". The removed `assert Process.alive?(self())` was vacuous; a test process asserting its own liveness inside itself can never fail. Deleting it is correct. Replacing the hand-shaped ctx map with a real Derive.context/3 result makes the fixture honest about the context shape. The error-return assertion is the real guard and it survived.

HOLDS -- modal_class_test contracted negatives. "mustn't" and "shan't" through punctuation normalization are genuine behavioral assertions on the cond-to-@modal_patterns rewrite. They would catch a botched \b boundary in the new regexes.

PROSE, NOT BEHAVIOR -- modal_class_test "documents the classifier as separate from the append-only gate". Stated plainly since you asked: all three assertions are text. Two read moduledoc and source with =~, and `refute source =~ "Regex.escape"` is a permanent ban on a stdlib function name appearing in that file. It maps to the spec statement this commit added (moduledoc wording, fixed module attributes), so it is not orphaned, but it proves nothing at runtime and will misfire if Regex.escape is ever needed there for an unrelated reason.

HOLDS -- next_test "uses a supplied status instead of rebuilding it". Genuinely discriminating. With status: %{subjects: []}, uncovered = [lib/sample.ex] and classification is "uncovered frontier change". If Next ignored the option and rebuilt, the sample.subject footprint covers lib/sample.ex, impacted is non-empty, and classification becomes "covered local change". Note it pins "uses the supplied status", not "builds status once" -- the once-only claim is carried by the prime_test trace.

PARTIAL -- base_view_test "materialize uses a cross-VM name and a non-recursive root mkdir". The AST scan does pin what the title says: reverting to the VM-local suffix drops cross_vm_suffix and fails; reverting File.mkdir to mkdir_p! makes the :mkdir count 0 and fails. Two gaps:
  1. The test never calls BaseView.materialize/3. The new {:error, {:temp_directory, reason}} branch in base_view.ex has no coverage at all, yet the spec says a pre-existing path "returns an error before any blob write". The final `assert {:error, :eexist} = File.mkdir(link)` characterizes Erlang and the OS, not Ancora.
  2. The count is on the :mkdir atom only. Adding File.mkdir_p!(temp_root) alongside the existing File.mkdir keeps the count at 1 and passes.

HOLDS WITH A GAP -- output_verdict_test "pass predicate honors explicit outcomes before finding counts". Four direct calls to Verdict.pass?/1, real behavior. %{pass: true, findings: [error]} pins pass beating a nonzero error count; %{fail: true} pins fail beating a zero count. Missing: %{fail: true, pass: true}. The spec statement this commit added says explicit fail takes precedence over explicit pass, and that ordering is not pinned by any assertion.

DOES NOT PIN DELEGATION -- output_verdict_test "gated output delegates to the verdict pass predicate". It greps lib/ancora/output.ex for the literal "Verdict.pass?(report)" and refutes "defp passed?". A duplicate predicate reintroduced under any other name (defp gate_passed?) alongside a retained Verdict.pass?(report) call passes. It also cannot show the call site is the one controlling Mix.raise. A behavioral version is cheap: feed Output.emit a report where a count-only predicate and Verdict.pass?/1 diverge, %{pass: true, findings: [error]}, and assert it does not raise. The spec now names pass?/1 as the sole predicate for both the emitter and the gated exit path, so this deserves a real assertion.

GENUINE STRENGTHENING -- forbidden_writer_test. Dropping stdout_call?/1 widens the scan to IO.puts(:stderr, ...), which is exactly what the production diff moved out of Config, Severity, and Trailer into Output.config_diagnostic/1. Reverting any of those three fails the test. Static source scan, no runtime dependency, nothing to verify by mutation. Blind spots remain -- it matches only IO.puts/write/inspect and Mix.shell, so IO.warn, :io.format, and Logger.* would slip -- but I grepped lib/ and none of those exist outside the Output modules today, so there is no live escape.

ACCEPTABLE, WITH A NOTE -- tmp_git_repo.exs cleanup poll removal. No test depends on the removed wait: all eight callers are inside on_exit and none assert on the return value or on the directory being gone. The old poll did not address the race it was blamed for anyway; it polled File.exists? after rm_rf, which is about deletion finishing, not about the git OS process exiting. So swapping it for Process.sleep(30) before rm_rf is not a loss of rigor. Two things to know: it is a bare timing constant with no observable event behind it (there is nothing to synchronize on once the port is closed), and cleanup! no longer retries, where it previously retried for up to a second, so a slow machine can now leave a temp dir behind.

Stderr race, measured on this tree. Three runs of all five files that call TmpGitRepo.cleanup! (git_batch_port_test, git_test, membership_test, change_set_test, base_view_test): 0, 0, 0 `fatal: not a git repository` lines, 28 tests 0 failures each time. Three runs of the five git-using files under review: 0, 0, 0 fatal, 30 tests 0 failures each. Matches the implementer's claim.

Full run of the ten files under review: 75 tests, 0 failures.

## UNVERIFIED BY READING

None outstanding. The three call_count assertions were the candidates, and I resolved them by running the tests to green -- a delta of exactly 1 cannot be produced by a trace mechanism that never fires, so passing is itself the reachability evidence. The one vacuity I found (review_test FindingsDelta refute) I confirmed by execution with a probe file, not by inference.
